transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because things have felt kind of out of control lately. I had just moved into a new apartment and could barely get settled, and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and trying to redesign my whole portfolio all at once. It felt like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint.
During that time, did you need much less sleep than usual?
Yes. For a few nights I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours, but I’d wake up feeling like I was totally fine. I remember thinking I should just use the extra time to get ahead.
During that time, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people probably couldn’t?
I don’t know if I’d say powerful. I felt more sure of myself than usual, like my ideas were really good and I could handle a lot, but not like I could do something nobody else could.
During that time, were you talking more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember people telling me I was talking nonstop or anything. I may have been more eager to explain my ideas, but I didn’t notice a big change in how much I was talking.
During that time, did you feel unusually upbeat or irritable for most of the day?

Yes. Earlier this month I felt almost electric, really upbeat, like everything was moving fast in a good way. But then I’d flip and get really irritated over small stuff, like snapping at a contractor or my sister because something was delayed. At the time it felt like they were blocking me on purpose, even though looking back it was probably not that serious.
During that time, were you getting distracted more easily than usual?
I’m not sure. I don’t really remember feeling especially distractible. I was focused on what I was doing, maybe jumping between things a bit, but I didn’t notice it as a big problem.
During that time, were you more active than usual, like taking on a lot more projects or staying constantly busy?

Yes, definitely. I went from barely getting settled into my new apartment to suddenly saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and deciding I needed to redesign my whole portfolio. It felt like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint.
During that time, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

Yes. I spent money in a way that really wasn’t like me. I bought these expensive light fixtures for the apartment, a bunch of design software add-ons, and even booked a last-minute flight for a trip I couldn’t actually afford. At the time it felt justified, but afterward I looked at my savings and realized I’d done real damage.
About how many days in a row did that unusually upbeat or irritable, high-energy period last?
It’s been about a month, since I moved into the apartment. It hasn’t felt like one single day, exactly, but this whole intense up-and-down, high-energy pattern has been going on since then.
During that high-energy period, did it cause serious problems in your life, like you couldn’t function at work or at home?

Yeah, it did start causing problems. I missed a design review at work, which is not normal for me, and I’ve been avoiding friends and family because I feel embarrassed. I’ve just seemed so scattered and unreliable lately.
During that high-energy period, did you have any experiences that other people said weren’t real, like hearing voices or being convinced of something others clearly disagreed with?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things, and I don’t think I was convinced of anything that other people said was completely unreal. It was more that I was keyed up and making bad decisions, but not like that.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day?

Yes. The heavier depressed stretches have been happening since the separation, about 11 months ago. Even before this recent move, I was having periods like that, and the move just made it feel sharper.
Have you ever had a time when these high-energy, reduced-sleep periods became so severe that you were hospitalized?
No, I’ve never been hospitalized for it. It’s caused problems, but it hasn’t gotten to that point.
